newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen easing with mild weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen easing with mild weather.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open down slightly Tuesday based on generation units in the West returning to service and forecasts of mild weather over the next 10 days, industry sources said.
"We seem to have established a pattern where we are in a slow drift downward," said on Houston-based futures trader.
In early over the counter talk, July Palo Verde (PV) was pegged at $27.25-27.40 per megawatt hour (MWh) from Monday's NYMEX July close at $27.63 per MWh.
July California Oregon Border (COB) was talked at $16.90-17.10 per MWh from Monday's NYMEX close at $17.21 per MWh.
"There is no new news, we continue to see generation come back in the West," the Houston trader said, adding that weather forecasts looked bearish for electricity.
Expectations of mild weather and a growing regional supply of power put a damper on both cash electricity and futures prices on Monday.
Over the weekend, two 550 megawatt (MW) coal-fired units in Wyoming, one at the Jim Bridger plant and one at Laramie River Station, were restarted after maintenance outages.

Also, the 1,221 MW unit 2 at Palo Verde nuclear station in Arizona was operatng at 86 percent of capacity as of early Tuesday during unplanned repairs to a main feedwater heater leak, which were expected to finish early Tuesday.

Southwest forecasts called for generally fair and dry conditions through Thursday with temperatures expected to be two to six degrees below normal. Clouds, showers and thunderstorms were possible across the region later in the week.
The Pacific Northwest was expected to see temperatures near to slightly below normal through to the early weekend, with scattered showers and thunderstorms during the period.
NYMEX July Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading down 1.5 cents at $2.125 per million British thermal units as of 1010 EDT.
